predictions.selection_reason: type check -> determines recursive merge -> may enable deep merge of attacker-controlled objects leading to prototype pollution
predictions.source_summary: The 'o' parameter (target object) and 'objects' parameter (source objects) are passed to the defaults function. Values come from function arguments without validation.
predictions.sink_summary: The function recursively merges properties into the target object 'o'. If attacker-controlled objects contain special properties like __proto__ or constructor, they could pollute the prototype chain.
predictions.guard_summary: The is-plain-object dependency (v0.1.0) may not properly detect prototype objects. No validation of property names or prototype pollution guards present. The for-own dependency iterates over own properties but recursive merge enables deep prototype pollution.
predictions.risk_pattern: Recursive merge of nested objects without prototype pollution protection allows attacker-controlled objects to modify Object.prototype through specially crafted property paths.
predictions.context_summary: The function performs deep merge of objects by recursively copying properties from source objects to target. The changed line enables recursive merging when both target and source values are objects.
unresolved_facts: Exact behavior of is-plain-object v0.1.0 regarding prototype object detection

top_sast_rules.cwe_name: Improperly Controlled Modification of Object Prototype Attributes ('Prototype Pollution')
top_sast_rules.description: Attacker-controlled object keys modify Object prototype attributes.
top_sast_rules.pattern: cwe-1321 prototype-pollution __proto__ constructor prototype object-key property-key merge assign recursive-merge
top_sast_rules.remediation: Reject prototype keys and use schema-constrained object updates.
